## Definition of Done

### Development

- [ ] The implementation satisfies the task description and acceptance criteria.
- [ ] The code follows the repository's architecture, conventions, and patterns.
- [ ] Input validation, error handling, and edge cases are covered.
- [ ] Appropriate tests have been added or updated.
- [ ] There is no unused code, debugging code, or unrelated refactor.
- [ ] Linting, type checking, builds, and local tests pass.
- [ ] Migrations and configuration changes are documented.
- [ ] API compatibility is preserved or breaking changes are documented.
- [ ] Relevant performance implications have been considered.
- [ ] Security and data privacy implications have been considered.

### QA

- [ ] The primary workflow has been verified.
- [ ] Negative, boundary, and invalid-input scenarios have been verified.
- [ ] Regression testing has been completed for affected areas.
- [ ] UI loading, empty, error, and success states have been verified when applicable.
- [ ] API status codes, response formats, validation, and errors have been verified when applicable.
- [ ] Relevant browser, device, or environment coverage has been verified.
- [ ] Every discovered defect has reproducible steps and a priority.
- [ ] No blocker or critical defect remains open.
- [ ] QA has confirmed that the acceptance criteria are satisfied.

### Code Review

- [ ] The reviewer understands the task goal and acceptance criteria.
- [ ] Correctness, security, error handling, and regressions have been reviewed.
- [ ] The impact on existing modules and integrations has been considered.
- [ ] Tests are meaningful and sufficient for the change.
- [ ] The code is readable and avoids unnecessary complexity.
- [ ] All blocking review comments have been resolved.
- [ ] Remaining non-blocking comments have been addressed or explicitly accepted.
- [ ] The reviewer has provided explicit approval.
- [ ] No unresolved change request remains.

### Documentation

- [ ] README, API documentation, or usage instructions have been updated when required.
- [ ] Configuration options and environment variables are documented.
- [ ] Migrations, deployment steps, and behavior changes are documented.
- [ ] Changelog or release notes have been updated when applicable.
- [ ] User-facing behavior is documented when appropriate.
- [ ] Documentation matches the actual implementation.
- [ ] Examples and code snippets have been verified.
